newsitem.title: FRANCE: EU aid chief urges Zaire force as refugees leave.
newsitem.headline: EU aid chief urges Zaire force as refugees leave.

text.p: European Union aid commissioner Emma Bonino on Monday urged the world to stick to plans to send a multinational force to Zaire, saying many Hutu refugees were still at risk despite an exodus home to Rwanda.

She estimated that 800,000 out of 1.2 million Hutu refugees threatened by a Tutsi rebellion in eastern Zaire were still in the country even though perhaps 400,000 had crossed the border back to Rwanda since late last week.

"Everything is as it was before," she told France Info radio, singling out the United States for dragging its feet over deployment of the force, which was sanctioned by the United Nations. "I think things have already been delayed too long."

"We have to be clear that the 400,000 people who have returned are from the Mugunga (refugee) camp" in eastern Zaire, she said. She added that the rest, who had fled other camps, "are still in the open in Zaire".
"I don't understand this renewed discussion about the multinational force," said Bonino, who last week accused the U.N. Security Council of scandalous indifference towards Zaire.
"I don't like having the impression that this American resistance to intervene is continuing for different reasons."

France, the first country to call for humanitarian intervention, and Canada, which offered to lead the force, said on Monday that the plans must go ahead. The U.N. agreed but the United States and other countries hinted they could drop out.
The U.S. military said a meeting in Germany of countries participating in the force for Zaire had been rescheduled to Thursday, a day later than originally planned.
